---
title: "Present and Defend: Visual Intelligence in Practice"
---

::: {.week-card}
**Core question:** Can students defend the whole product?
:::

## Learning focus

- group showcase
- individual oral defence
- defending user stories, Visual Vocabulary choices, code, data, deployment, disclosure, and AI use
- final reflection

## Three-hour structure

| Segment | Activity |
|---|---|
| Hour 1 | Concept, examples, and discussion |
| Hour 2 | Build, classify, or test |
| Hour 3 | Critique, review, repair, or studio output |

## Studio output

- Present the final app and complete individual oral defence.

## Visual Vocabulary prompt

```text
User story:
Visualisation purpose:
FT Visual Vocabulary category:
Chosen visual form:
Why this fits the task:
What could mislead:
Simpler alternative considered:
```

## Responsibility checkpoint

```text
Who is represented?
Who benefits from this visualisation?
Who could be harmed or misled?
What limitation must be disclosed?
What did intelligent tools help with, and how was the output checked?
```

## Relevant references

- Bearman et al., “Developing Evaluative Judgement for a Time of Generative AI”
- Sotiriadou et al., “The Role of Authentic Assessment to Preserve Academic Integrity”
- Dawson et al., “Validity Matters More Than Cheating”
